item.title: Iceblade of Narin: The Icebind: Hotfix 44.1.3
item.description:
Arsenal Retuning Inbox Message
This hotfix brings changes to Ammo Efficiency, Riven Mods, and hot-off-the-presses Acid Shell interactions, so all players who log in after today’s update will receive the following (until December 31st 2026 at 11:59pm ET):

  • 2 Built Forma + 100,000 Kuva
  • NOTE: To ensure all players receive the inbox as intended, it will be delivered at 3:30pm ET. 

Players who have installed a Riven Splicer in a Riven Mod prior to today’s hotfix will also receive the following in a separate inbox as a thank you for being an early adopter:

  • 1 Riven Splicer + 100,000 Kuva
  • NOTE: This inbox requires a script to run, which we will do shortly after the hotfix launches. 

Ammo Efficiency Changes
Our recent introduction of Ammo Efficiency traits to Riven mods via Riven Splicers has made this stat more accessible to players, and led to much discussion internally on how the availability of infinite ammo builds affects Warframe’s game balance. 

Warframe is about the power fantasy, and infinite ammo is the epitome of that. Shooting endlessly into hordes of enemies can feel incredible, and we want players to be able to experience that — sometimes. The recent introduction of Riven Splicers has changed that “sometimes” for infinite ammo into a much more guaranteed thing, which has brought around this the following changes:

  • Ammo Efficiency is now capped at 75%. 
    • For those unfamiliar with the Ammo Efficiency mechanic, this means only 1 in 4 shots will consume ammo. 
    • This applies to Ammo Efficiency increases from multiple sources — they will only increase the stat up to this cap. 
    • The Ammo Efficiency cap applies to all equipment that uses Ammo, including Necramechs and Amps.
  • Sources that intentionally gave 100% Ammo Efficiency (ex: Void Relic cracking buffs) have now been rephrased to indicate they give Infinite Ammo.
  • There are other Mods, Arcanes, and Incarnon Evolutions that come with their own edge-cases, which we’ll explain in detail below.

Sources of Infinite Ammo
These mechanics remain unchanged, but their buff descriptions have been updated to specify that they give Infinite Ammo

  • Void Relic Cracking Buffs
  • Akmagnus Prime and Magnus Prime unique trait: Chamber Cascade
  • Athodai (Prime) unique trait: Overdrive
  • Dual Toxocyst unique trait: Frenzy
  • Knell (Prime) unique trait: Death Knell
  • Perigale (Prime) unique trait: Gale Force
  • Vasto Incarnon evolution: Reaper’s Plenty

Changes to Sources of Ammo Efficiency

  • AX-52:
    • Was: Hip-fired shots have +60% Ammo Efficiency.
    • Now: Hip-fired shots have +75% Ammo Efficiency.
  • Eternal Logistics: 
    • Note: the following change is a minor buff to the Arcane as its max rank Ammo Efficiency value was just below the cap. 
    • Was: On Void Sling:+72% Amp Ammo Efficiency for 8s
    • Now: On Void Sling: +75% Amp Ammo Efficiency for 8s 
  • Arcane Pistoleer
    • Was: On Pistol Weak Point Kill: 60% chance for +102% (+17% at Unranked) Ammo Efficiency for 12s
    • Now: On Pistol Weak Point Kill: 60% (10% at Unranked) Chance for Infinite Ammo for 12s
  • Brain Storm Augment (Grakata)
    • Was: On Headshot: +100% (25% at Unranked) Ammo Efficiency for 0.5s (0.125s at Unranked)
    • Now: On Headshot: 40% (10% at Unranked) Chance for Infinite Ammo for 2s (0.5s at Unranked)
  • Skull Shots Augment (Viper)
    • Was: On Headshot: 100% Ammo Efficiency (25% at Unranked) for 2.0s (0.5s at Unranked)
    • Now: On Headshot: 40% Chance for Infinite Ammo (10% chance at Unranked) for 2.0s (0.5s at Unranked)
  • Incarnon Evolution “Enough for Everyone” (Bronco)
    • Was: +80% Ammo efficiency when 6 enemies are within 6m.
    • Now: +75% Ammo efficiency when 6 enemies are within 6m.
  • Incarnon Evolution “Crimson Overture” (Dera and Boltor)
    • Was: On Kill: +20% Ammo Efficiency for 5 seconds. Stacks up to 4x.
    • Now: On Kill: +25% Ammo Efficiency for 5 seconds. Stacks up to 3x.
    • Note: the increase to Base Damage is unchanged.
  • Lyon’s “Flowing Slayer” blessing in The Descendia
    • Was: Gain +90% Ammo Efficiency while Sliding or Crouching, but receive -30% Ammo Efficiency otherwise.
    • Now: Gain +75% Ammo Efficiency while Sliding or Crouching, but receive -25% Ammo Efficiency otherwise.
    • Also fixed this Blessing not applying properly in-mission.

Recursive “Explode on Death” Changes
Acid Shells has been a hot topic of late — for those unaware, it’s a Sobek Augment that causes enemies to explode on death and deals radial damage that scales with enemy health. Alone, it’s powerful, but it was made even more so via a niche interaction with Elemental Ammo, most commonly used with Cyte-09 (but also seen with Grendel, Oraxia, and Saryn, among others). These Elemental Ammo upgrades could cause Acid Shells to recursively trigger — meaning the one-time death explosion from a shot could instead be triggered infinitely if there were enough enemies to sustain it.

This build type has been on our radar for a while, but we didn’t feel it was the right time to address it. As developers, we’ve been pretty transparent about our threshold to “nerf” content; the Cyte-09 and Acid Shells build never felt dominant or disruptive enough to warrant a closer look, but over the past few weeks that has changed. Arbitrations, discussions about Ammo Efficiency, and the introduction of the Epoch Operation: Taubound have rapidly increased the popularity of this build, to the point where we feel we need to address it.

For the sake of consistency, we have reviewed all death detonation effects as part of the following changes, since this mechanic is not unique to Acid Shells: 

  • Fixed status effects caused by Elemental Ammo on “enemies explode on death” effects being able to retrigger the death explosion effects for the following Mods:
    • Note: these Mods will still benefit from increased damage and status effects gained from Elemental Ammo — they just won’t retrigger the death effects infinitely.
    • Acid Shells
    • Amalgam Furax Body Count
    • Vulcan Blitz
    • Explosive Demise
    • Combustion Beam
    • Thermagnetic Shells
    • Entropy Detonation
  • Reduced Acid Shells’ explosion radius from 15m to 10m.

Riven Mod Changes
First introduced alongside the launch of Rivens in 2016, Riven Dispositions were internal multipliers that guided how strong Rivens would be on individual weapons — ranging from 0.5 on popular weapons, up to 1.55 on those lesser-used.  

The intent of these Dispositions was to incentivize players to use less powerful weapons, but ultimately we saw that investment was still focused on making powerful weapons more powerful. Incarnons were a more successful attempt at breathing life into older outdated weapons, and the overlapping of these systems only multiplied their power further.

With all that in mind, we are making the following change:

  • Removed Riven Dispositions.
    • All Rivens now use the same multiplier for their possible value ranges, the equivalent of 1.2 Disposition in the old system.
    • For more information on the history behind this decision, please review our Dev Workshop. 
  • Restored the ability to trade Riven Mods.

General Additions & Changes 

  • Added the new Axi C13 Relic to mission drop tables to address the Braton Prime Receiver unintentionally being vaulted.
  • The search function in the Peely Pix menu now also searches Peely Pix descriptions.
  • Credit Bundles now have a multiple purchase option (notably for the Credit Bundles in Praghasa's wares).

Fixes

  • Fixed casting the Void of the Lotus ability with specific controller inputs causing players to experience extreme slow mode in the Lua quest.
  • Fixed the Vessel's Gaze dealing no damage if the ability was used before a specific segment in the Vessel quest.
  • Fixed being unable to chatlink Riven Splicers.
  • Fixed the Security Bypass terminal waypoint disappearing once Yareli mounts Merulina.
  • Fixed performance issues caused by Yareli casting Jade Stars while on Merulina.
  • Fixed the gas clouds spawned by Toxic Amphors dealing damage to players.
  • Fixed the Adarza and Smeeta Kavats missing their hair tufts.
  • Fixed the Lotus' Epoch Operation: Taubound inbox message not specifying that Praghasa is found on Eris.
  • Fixed upgrading Boreal's Hatred sometimes displaying incorrect stats if certain Numerical Separator settings were applied.
  • Fixed subtitles for a certain character during the Lua quest not indicating they are a foe.
  • Fixed rare cases of players not receiving the Vessel quest key upon completion of the Lua quest in the Prologue to Tau series. 
    • A small number of players were affected by this issue, and should see the missing quest key in their inventories.
  • Fixed the End of Mission cinematic zooming in too closely to the squad in The Icebind.
  • Fixed being unable to use Fast Travel while in the hallway leading to the Dark Refractory in the Sanctum Anatomica.
  • Fixed ambient music not stopping when returning to the Mountain Pass in The War Within quest.

Script Error Fixes:
Script errors mean that something went wrong when the game client was executing a script, which can have various outcomes. Usually it means the related content didn’t function properly under specific circumstances — often we don’t actually know what the error outcome was, so we list it as a Script Error fix to indicate it was addressing an unintended behaviour.

  • Fixed a script error related to Market search sorting.
  • Fixed a script error caused by the electric traps in the Kuva Fortress tileset.
  • Fixed a script error related to the Belfri Ephemera.

For a list of known issues that are on our radar, visit our dedicated thread: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1523875-known-issues-iceblade-of-narin

item.title: Iceblade of Narin: The Icebind: Hotfix 44.1.4
item.description:
Changes

  • Reduced the Nami Skyla Prime Blade's Ducat value from 100 to 65 as a result of its varied rarity from Void Relics.
  • The Skull Shots Augment (Viper) can now retrigger its buff while it is currently active.
  • Added the option "Make Spawn Room" to the following Dojo rooms (at room console)
    • Duviri Cave
    • Earth Forest Chamber
    • Galleon Chamber
    • Infested Chamber
    • Kuva Asteroid
    • Orokin Tower Chamber
    • Ostron Cove
    • Starlight Market
    • Uranus Chamber

Fixes

  • Fixed cases of The Icebind Mobile Defense missions not properly extracting due to a specific tile in the Grineer Asteroid tileset.
  • Fixed players who have not unlocked Eris being unable to see or play the Epoch Operation: Taubound Alerts.
  • Fixed Amanata Pressure not applying to Heavy Slam Attacks.
    • Also fixed Amanata Pressure only affecting one enemy per Heavy Attack.
  • Fixed an Incarnon's reticle turning blue before its transformation into an Incarnon is complete, sometimes leading players to interrupt transformation prematurely.
  • Fixed the Vasto Incarnon's "Reaper's Plenty" evolution missing its hud buff icon when triggered.
  • Fixed a case of Sirius & Orion losing function if you swapped between a Son at a specific moment when travelling through a Sanctuary Onslaught portal.
  • Fixed extracting from Zariman missions during Last Gasp potentially breaking active abilities in future missions started from Chrysalith
  • Fixed loud SFX playing if players used Front Artillery while the Railjack was boosting with the "Fire Manual Trigger Weapons Continuously" toggled on.
  • Fixed pickups being able to spawn in an inaccessible area in a specific Lua tile. 
  • Fixed various shoulder armor offset issues for Caliban Prime.
  • Fixed offset issues for the Spritsail Prime Shoulder Guards on Citrine Prime.
  • Fixed a crash related to Voice Chat.
  • Fixed a missing "+" in Energized Munition's description.
  • Fixed Rusalka's hair appearing too brown in The Hex quest.
  • Fixed a rare case of Nidus' Parasitic Vitality being able to kill Nidus or crash the game. 
  • Fixed Teshin missing animations during a specific segment of The New War quest.
  • Fixed Valkyr's Warcry hud buff icon remaining active after being Valkyr is Nullified (via a Nullifier bubble, etc.).

Script Error Fixes:
Script errors mean that something went wrong when the game client was executing a script, which can have various outcomes. Usually it means the related content didn’t function properly under specific circumstances — often we don’t actually know what the error outcome was, so we list it as a Script Error fix to indicate it was addressing an unintended behaviour.

  • Fixed a script error related to transmissions, notably those from Vena.
  • Fixed a script error in the input binding menu.
  • Fixed a script error related to the Dark Refractory screen.
  • Fixed a script error related to "explode on kill" effects.

For a list of known issues that are on our radar, visit our dedicated thread: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1523875-known-issues-iceblade-of-narin/

item.title: Iceblade of Narin: The Icebind: Hotfix 44.1.2 + 2.1
item.description:
Iceblade of Narin: The Icebind: Hotfix #2.1

Fixes:

  • Fixed crashing and/or severe performance issues when entering The Dark Refractory as part of the Lua quest in the Prologue to Tau. 

For a list of known issues that are on our radar, visit our dedicated thread:  https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1523875-known-issues-iceblade-of-narin/

Iceblade of Narin: The Icebind: Hotfix #2

Image Description: A Vessel stands in the middle of an infested landscape, staring away from the viewer and towards the sky. The Vessel is a large bald unclothed humanoid with carved lines across his skin. A Warframe hovers over their right shoulder, appearing to be slightly larger than its ear, showcasing the scale of the Vessel. Praghasa is in the sky, peeking through clouds and infested tendrils. 

Tau Prologue Quest Series
A series of new Prologue Quests are available in the Codex! 

These short Prologue Quests set the stage for the start of our journey. Players who have completed both The Hex and The Old Peace quests will see the Tau Prologue Series in their Codex upon login. 

These Prologue Chapters are a permanent addition to the Main Story, and are replayable. 

The road to Tau is long, Tenno. But together, we’re finally going!

Epoch Operation: Taubound - Begins at 11:00 AM ET!
Launching alongside this hotfix is a new once in a Star Chart Operation, Epoch Operation: Taubound. This community event forms part of the preparation for us to make the journey to Tau.

For a full breakdown of the event and what to expect please read our dedicated post here: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1528603-epoch-operation-taubound/.

Changes:

  • Added a shortcut to the Riven Splicing menu while on the Riven Cycling screen.
  • Updated the on-hover Lock Riven Trait description to specify that Locking a trait also locks the number of positive and negative traits when cycling.
  • Reduced the Bronco Prime Barrel's Ducat price from 45 to 25 due to changes in its rarity from Void Relics.

 

The Icebind Changes & Fixes:

  • Added SFX to various elements in The Icebind, including SFX for connecting and reconnecting a Signal Bridge, and more.
  • Fixed cases of returning players from a Host Migration not being transported to the treasure room if the mission objective was completed and extraction was paused due to an active Side Objective.
    • Now, the active Side Objective will be cancelled for returning players so they can properly extract.
    • Also fixed cases of returning hosts loading into a mission by themselves instead of the treasure room with the rest of their squad.
  • Fixed certain Mars Excavation Cryobells resulting in players not being teleported to The Icebind's treasure room if the final Side Objective was Cryothermia.
  • Fixed issues with the “Take Cryobell” context action.

Top Fixes:

  • Fixed Ash marking enemies with Bladestorm and then using Transference causing the marks to remain, but Bladestorm not being performed on them.
  • Fixed Client Chroma's Elemental Ward element always being Heat, regardless of emissive tint.
  • Fixed Nova's Wormhole spawning far from her if it's aimed directly upwards.
  • Fixed Secondary Enervate being able to proc infinitely off of Zephyr's Tornados.

Fixes:

  • Fixed Uriel's Infernum Augment using the incorrect SFX for the explosion sounds.
  • Fixed a [PH] appearing next to Slam Damage in the Riven Splicing menu.
  • Fixes towards the desaturated areas on the Saryn Velenosa Skin becoming vibrant following our metal shader changes.
  • Fixed Citrine Prime's shoulder attachment offsets being asymmetrical.
  • Fixed material issues on the Harrow Profitas Helmet.
  • Fixed being able to own multiple copies of the Kyzen and Karotic Signas.
  • This offered no benefit to players, other than cluttering their list of Signas in customization menus!
  • Fixed the glass in the Personal Quarters appearing almost white on lower spec devices.
  • Fixed Commandeered Volt Prime's electrical beam VFX not being removed after the ability ends.
  • Fixed an additional rare case of Inaros being revived with function loss if he died at the start of casting Sandstorm with an item (ex: Power Cell) in his hands.
  • Fixed a map hole in the Yuvan Peak Captura Scene.
  • Fixed various blocking volumes appearing in The War Within Choice Captura scene.
  • Fixed the Circuit "Choose Your Path" screen overlapping the friends menu if you join a Friend's Circuit session in progress without yet having chosen your weekly path.
  • Fixed opening a Chatlinked item while in the "Ring a Cryobell" screen causing the menus to overlap.

Script Error Fixes:
Script errors mean that something went wrong when the game client was executing a script, which can have various outcomes. Usually it means the related content didn’t function properly under specific circumstances — often we don’t actually know what the error outcome was, so we list it as a Script Error fix to indicate it was addressing an unintended behaviour.

  • Fixed a script error caused by resource containers exploding from Mirage's Sleight of Hand while she is dead.
  • Fixed a script error caused by Jade's Symphony of Mercy going on cooldown (ex: in a Sanctuary Onslaught mission).
  • Fixed a script error when hovering over pop-ups.
  • Fixed a script crash at the end of the Surge Eximus' speed ability.
  • Fixed a script error in the Operator/Drifter loadout menu.
  • Fixed a script error in a Warframe's Configuration screen in Teshin's Cave in Duviri.
  • Fixed a script error when backing out of a menu.
  • Fixed a script error related to buff notifications.
  • Fixed a script error when hovering over different categories in the Railjack menu.

For a list of known issues that are on our radar, visit our dedicated thread: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1523875-known-issues-iceblade-of-narin/

item.title: Update 44.1.0: Iceblade of Narin: The Icebind
item.description:
Image Description: Six Warframes stand poised for battle within a frosty cave with the Warframe logo and The Icebind: New 6 Player Missions in the foreground. From left to right we can see: Wisp, Rhino, Volt, Excalibur, Mesa, and Mag.

UPDATE 44.1: ICEBLADE OF NARIN: THE ICEBIND

Time for an experiment, students! What happens if you ring that bell?

Our newest gamemode has arrived! The Icebind is an experiment for both us making Warframe, and for those playing it. This new mode aims to give players space to push their loadout and tackle cooperative objectives — as the community rings their Cryobells, we’ll be watching for feedback as we continue to iterate on this project in phases.

NEW GAMEMODE: THE ICEBIND
The Icebind is manifested through the Cryobell ceremony. High upon Yuvan Peak, Cryobells have formed, drawn out by Narin’s influence. Each bell's tone leads to a time and place where a dark influence has taken hold. Six warriors must gather to ring the bell. Together they must overcome the Binds of a force not of this plane.

General Overview for The Icebind:

Players can ring a Cryobell to take them to The Icebind, a new mission type with these key characteristics:

  • Six player squads, where there can be no more than one of each Warframe.
    • (i.e. no six man Pink Rhino Squads this time, sorry!)
  • Approximately 10-15 minute long missions. 
  • Level 999+ Enemies.
  • Each Cryobell (mission key) comes with a randomized mission type, enemy, location, and modifiers — the squad votes on which one to play!
  • Various mission restrictions, including No Self Revives, Gear Cooldown Increase, Empowered Enemies, and more.
  • Guaranteed Riven Splicer upon completion, plus an additional reward from the reward pool.
  • Bonus rewards for each Squad Side Objective completed (up to 3 per mission).
  • Players can complete these missions three times a week.*
    • * players can stockpile up to six mission keys if they do not use them all each week.

To access The Icebind, players must have completed the following: 

  • Completed both the Angels of the Zariman and Whispers in the Walls quests
  • Unlocked (but not necessarily completed) either Elite Temporal Archimedea or Elite Deep Archimedea

The Core Icebind Loop
The Icebind is different each time a player steps into it, beholden to the randomized traits of the Cryobell. Before we explain the various Binds (i.e. modifiers) introduced by the Cryobells, it’s important to understand the core gameplay loop. This section explains the overarching structure of playing The Icebind, and the section following will outline the various Binds that can affect it. 

Starting The Icebind
This new mission can be started from Yuvan Peak, where players need to perform two important steps:

  • First, claim their Cryobells from the ice pillar atop Yuvan Peak.
    • Three Cryobells form each week, following weekly reset at Midnight UTC on Sundays.
    • Players can stockpile up to six Cryobells if they did not use them all in one week.
  • Second, with Cryobells in-hand, speak to Cephalon Melica and select “Ring a Cyrobell”

Image Description: Screenshot of Narin standing in front of Cephalon Melica at the Yuvan Peak. The context action UI for Cephalon Melica can be seen, with large ice pillars covered in talismans on either side behind the Cephalon.

Doing so will open The Icebind party creation screen, where you can invite players to form your squad. The host can only form a six player squad using the “Ring the Cryobell” screen. With its launch, The Icebind does not have public matchmaking as these missions require more cooperation than traditional Warframe missions (which we’ll cover a little more in the Squad Side Objective section). 

SELECTING A CRYOBELL
Players who are invited to a Squad will be summoned to Yuvan Peak, where they can then gather their Cryobells and proceed to Cephalon Melica. All players must speak to Cephalon Melica and select “Ring a Cryobell” to start the mission. 

In this screen, players can edit their loadout and select which Cryobell they wish to ring. Your choice of Cryobell matters, because it determines your Personal Bind (which is a guaranteed personal modifier for the mission, regardless of which Cryobell is chosen by the squad) and which version of The Icebind players will vote on (including the mission type, enemy type, and modifiers). 

Image Description: Screenshot of the Select Cryobell UI showing three Cryobells and some of their traits. From left to right we see: a Disruption on Earth against the Corpus, a Mobile Defense on Ceres against The Murmur, and an Excavation on Pluto against the Orokin.

When selecting a Cryobell, you’ll be able to see each of the traits it will give to your mission:

  • Mission Type 
  • Planet
  • Enemy Type
  • Mission Bind
  • Tactical Bind
  • Personal Bind

We’ll go over all of these randomized traits in the “Cryobells and their Binds” section of this Dev Workshop.

After all players have selected a Cryobell, the entire squad can vote on which one to play! 

VOTING ON A CRYOBELL
Once all players have selected a Cryobell, a 60 second voting countdown begins. Players can review all of the available mission options available to them, and vote on which one to play! If no votes are cast, a random Cryobell is chosen; in the case of a tie, the Host’s vote is the deciding choice. 

 Image Description: Screenshot of The Icebind UI after each player has selected their Cryobell and are voting on the mission. From left to right we can see your current loadout and each players’ Cryobell traits. Underneath we see icons for Standard Mission Traits, the mission start timer, your Personal Bind, and the option to view Rewards.

Once voting concludes, players have an additional 10 second countdown to review the selected Cryobell before the mission begins. 

While Cryobells are consumable mission keys, rest assured Cryobells are not spent until players have successfully extracted from The Icebind. 

Playing The Icebind
Entering the Icebind, you’ll be starting a mission as you normally would — as normal as it can be, considering randomized Binds of a Cryobell. Players will be presented with either a Survival, Mobile Defense, Excavation, or Disruption mission depending on the chosen Cryobell. At the beginning, you’ll be prompted to start your objective and aim to complete it successfully, with bonus Squad Side Objectives spawning in at regular intervals to keep things interesting. We’ll get to those in a bit!

While many elements of The Icebind are random, there are guaranteed elements you can expect each time you play.

STANDARD MISSION TRAITS

  • Enemy Level: 999+
  • Guaranteed Reward: Riven Splicer (plus Kuva and an additional reward from the Reward Pool after opening a Crested Chest)
  • No Duplicate Warframes: Only one of each Warframe can enter the mission. 
  • Mission Restrictions:
    • Empowered Enemies: Enemy Health and Shields and Armor increased by 200% and an additional 100% for each squad member, stacking to a maximum of 800%. Increased chance of Eximus. 
    • No Self Revive: After a Tenno has bled-out, a Tombstone will appear where they fell. At least 3 surviving Tenno must sacrifice part of their health temporarily to bring the Tenno back into the action. If fewer than 3 Tenno are still standing then all of them must make the sacrifice to revive others.
    • Last Gasp Penalty: Activating the Last Gasp focus ability reduces the timer by 2 seconds.
    • Bleedout Shortens: The bleedout timer shortens after each revive, to a minimum of 5 seconds.
    • Frozen Keys: After being dead for 3 minutes you will not obtain any Frozen Keys that the squad acquires from completing objectives while you are dead. 
    • Cooldown Increase: Each type of Restore has a 3 minute cooldown timer applied. 
    • Fatigued Companions: Companion Recovery timer increased by 100%.
    • Stunted Shields: Full Shield Gate immunity duration reduced by 50%. 

As the mission progresses, Squad Side Objectives begin to spawn for a total of 3 per mission. 

Look for the purple waypoint on your minimap indicating a Squad Side Objective is available. These side objectives are optional, but completing them gives the squad extra rewards!

HOW TO START AN OPTIONAL SQUAD SIDE OBJECTIVE
Depending on the objective, a certain number of Squad members are required to be nearby before it can be even started. This is important, because failing a Squad Side Objective will fail your mission and require you to start again. Choosing to do Side Squad Objectives is a matter of risk vs reward — do you trust your squad to succeed, and in return earn a Frozen Key to unlock more rewards? Or will you decide to not start the Squad Side Objectives and just earn the guaranteed Riven Splicer and completion reward upon mission success?

To ensure these are not started until players are ready, the Side Objective must be activated via a “Start” prompt, which then updates the objective description to indicate how many players need to be nearby. Once enough players are in the area, the objective will begin! Through teamwork, you all must work together to complete your task within the allotted time.

With The Icebind’s launch, there are 5 Squad Side Objectives to master:

  • Lockbox: collect Cyphers from fallen enemies and bring them to the Lockbox to unlock it.
  • Cryothermia: neutralize a Cryo Core by holding it while it deals escalating damage to player health.
  • Indomitable Ice: charge ice crystals with concentrated fire.
  • Entropy Orb: gather around the orb and avoid its damaging pulses.
  • Signal Chain: connect a beam of energy between one point to another using your Warframes.

Successfully completing a Squad Side Objective rewards all squad members with a Frozen Key, which can be used to unlock rewards in a special treasure room upon mission completion. 

Since players can try to tackle 3 of these objectives in one mission, time management is another factor to master! Rest assured, if you are rushing to complete your final Squad Side Objective before the mission ends, the mission will not extract players if there is an active Squad Side Objective*. Once that is complete, you’ll be whisked away to the end of mission screen (whether that’s a mission fail or mission success is up to your performance). 

* Specifically, if the Squad Side Objective has had the "Start" input pressed — not just the waypoint appearing on the map.

MELICA’S GLACIAL LABORATORY
The Icebind doesn’t end with the usual race towards extraction. Instead, once the mission is complete, players will be immediately transported to Melica’s Glacial Laboratory. Here, they can use their earned Keys to unlock chests and collect what was earned. Players are also rewarded a guaranteed Riven Splicer upon mission completion! Learn more about Riven Splicing in our dedicated section below.

There are two different Keys that are earned in The Icebind:

  • Crested Frozen Key — guaranteed reward for completing the mission
  • Frozen Key — earned by completing Squad Side Objectives, up to 3 can be obtained per mission

Crested Frozen Keys open Crested Chests, which appear at the center of the map. Full drop rates can be found on our official Droptable Site.

Crested Frozen Key Rewards:

  • Guaranteed Kuva:
    • 7,500 Kuva
    • 17,500 Kuva
    • 100,000 Kuva
  • Additional Reward Table:

Frozen Keys open Frozen Chests, which can be found on the outside edges of the map. Full drop rates can be found on our official Droptable Site. 

Frozen Key Rewards:

  • Guaranteed Kuva:
    • 1,750 Kuva
    • 3,500 Kuva
    • 7,500 Kuva
  • Additional Reward Table:
    • Forma
    • 200 Vosfor
    • 3 Day Affinity Booster
    • 3 Day Resource Drop Chance Booster
    • 3 Day Resource Booster
    • 3 Day Credit Booster

    • Pistol Riven Mod
    • Rifle Riven Mod
    • Shotgun Riven
    • Azure Archon Shard
    • Crimson Archon Shard
    • Amber Archon Shard

Once you’ve unlocked your Chests, you can proceed to the marked extraction point. That said, there are more than just rewards to be found in Melica’s Glacial Laboratory — curious Tenno may wish to search the room for fragments from the distant past.

Image Description: An image of a default Liset Landing Craft, with a Cryobell placed on the nose of the ship where Sumdalis are equipped. The Cryobell appears as a glowing core with six crystallized offshoots all around it.

First-Time Completion Reward

Completing The Icebind for the first time also rewards players with a Cryobell Sumdali, as proof that they have overcome the Binds of a force not of this plane.
 

Image Description: Banshee Threnodia looks at three Cryobells that have emerged from an ice pillar covered in talismans in the Yuvan Peak. Each Cryobell appears as a glowing core with six crystallized offshoots all around it.
Cryobells and their Binds
Now that you should have a basic understanding of the core loop when playing The Icebind, it’s time to talk about the Cryobells. Formed through Narin’s influence on Yuvan Peak, each bell’s tone leads to a time and place where a dark influence has taken hold, manifesting as different Binds that alter the player’s experience. 

Bound to each Cryobell is a randomized set of traits, which determines the mission it will take you to:

  • Mission Type
  • Mission Location
  • Enemy Type
  • Personal Bind
  • Mission Bind
  • Tactical Bind

Let’s go over what each of these can be! 

Mission Type

  • Survival (10 Minutes)
  • Mobile Defense (3 Terminals of 3 minutes each)
  • Excavation (600 Cryotic)
  • Disruption (8 Conduits)

Mission Location

  • Any Planet in the Origin System, excluding Duviri, The Dark Refractory, and Höllvania. 

Enemy Type

  • Grineer
  • Corpus
  • Infested
  • The Murmur
  • Orokin

Personal Bind
Your Cryobell’s Personal Bind applies to you in-mission, regardless of what Cryobell was chosen by the Squad. 

  • Abbreviated Abilities: Ability durations reduced by 50%.
  • Ability Overload: Using an ability opens a void rift nearby.
  • Ammo Deficit: Ammo restored by drops and gear is reduced by 75%
  • Constricted: Max energy reduced by 75%. 
  • Dark Antimatter: Enemies slain by ability damage create a hostile antimatter drop that is attracted to you. 
  • Dropped Guard: Warframe and ally Overguard* gain reduced by 75%. 
    • *Overguard gained from Allies, this Bind does not affect your squadmates’ Overguard.
  • Dull Blades: -50% melee combo chance. 
  • Energy Exhaustion: Lose 2 Energy per second for each enemy within 10 meters of you.
  • Firewalker: For each meter travelled on foot, take increasing heat damage over time. Jumping or being airborne reduces it.
  • Flankable: Max shield capacity is reduced by 75%, but an impenetrable Volt shield is permanently in front of you. 
  • Fractured Armor: Casting an ability reduces armor by 10% for 10s.
  • Framecurse Syndrome: Activating an Ability inflicts 50 health and 150 shield damage upon you.
  • Hypersensitive: Duration of negative Status Effects is tripled
  • Knifestep Syndrome: Lose 2 Health when moving. Jumping pauses the effect.
  • Lethargic Shields: Shield recharge delay increased 500%.
  • Performance Anxiety: A spotlight chases you. Killing enemies while illuminated inflicts damage on you that increases with each kill. 
  • Permanent Injury: Max health reduced each time health damage is taken
  • Secondary Wounds: Gain 1 Puncture Status Effect every time you take damage.
  • Shocking Leaps: Jumping or Bullet Jumping generates a Shock Eximus orb that chases you. 
  • Slam Spikes: Melee Slam Attacks cause damaging spikes to erupt from the ground for 2s after the slam.
  • Static Siphon: Casting abilities causes all enemies within 15m to emit damaging electrical chains back to the caster.
  • Undersupplied: Max ammo on all weapons reduced by 75%
  • Untreatable: Pickups do not heal, and Health Orbs cannot be picked up. 

Mission Bind
A Mission Bind is a complication that alters the entire theme of the mission. These introduce gameplay elements to work around, and can affect what type of units spawn.

  • Entropic Overload: Using abilities spawns Entropic Crystals on you and triggers Entropic Overload, causing enemies to self-revive as Leech Eximus and hostile Entropic Wisps appear. Getting hit by a Wisp causes stacked crystals to explode. Destroying Entropic Crystals and Wisps will decrease saturation. 
  • Stone Soldiers: Enemies are hard as stone and hit even harder. Taking them by surprise is the best way to exploit weak points in their stony flesh. In addition, you will face hostile Tomb Guardians.
  • Miasmic Militia: Enemies slowly take damage, but are immune to Toxin, Gas, Viral, and Corrosive status effects. On death, a Gas cloud is released.
  • Thin Boundary: Void Tears rip into reality, growing with nearby ability use. Tears inflict Void Shackles, reducing ability stats and weapon combo durations, while draining energy, health, and Incarnon weapon energy.
  • Inferno: Heat Status present on players or enemies will feed the Inferno, drawing in Arson Eximus, Heat empowered enemies, and damaging anyone near active sources of Heat. Avoid inflicting Heat Status and killing hostile Heat sources to starve the Inferno. 

Tactical Bind
A Tactical Bind is an additional complication that may affect your loadout or gameplay decisions. 

  • Antimatter Foes: Enemies killed by abilities spawn a hostile Antimatter Drop that tracks you.
  • Archaic Armor: Enemy armor is greatly increased and cannot be stripped normally. Each hit they take reduces their maximum armor by 1%.
  • Bruised Shields: Shields can only be restored via melee attacks.
  • Bolstered Belligerents: All enemies have Overguard equal to 50% of their max health.
  • Clumsy Munitions: When taking damage, a grenade may be dropped at your feet that explodes after a few seconds.
  • Cumulonimbus: Being airborne triggers cumulative electrical damage, which dissipates over time once on the ground.
  • Entanglement: Allies within 4m of slain enemies endure reduced Movement Speed and Parkour Velocity. 
  • Heavy Warfare: Enemies take -90% less damage from non-heavy weapons. Enemies will drop heavy ammo packs and heavy weapon recall time reduced to 5 sec.
  • Jade Spirits: Jade Wisps haunt the region. If approached, they chase down the player responsible and transform into Jade Light beams. 
  • Kela's Revenge: Missiles strike from above periodically.
  • Myopic Munitions: Enemies will only take damage if a player is within 15m of them.
  • Parasitic Light: The squad is given two parasitic lanterns which drain energy of those that carry them. Enemies outside the lanterns’ light have massive damage reduction.
  • Postmortal Surges: Slain enemies explode with Void energy.
  • Toasty Toes: Grounded movement inflicts Heat damage over time. Airborne movement reduces it.

How you choose to counteract these Binds is up to you, as The Icebind does not come with specific loadout restrictions. 

For feedback on The Icebind game mode, please use the dedicated The Icebind subforum.

 Image Description: An image of a Riven Splicer, which is a technological device. It is a trapezoidal shape, with three arms jutting off, which point to the center in the shape of a triangle. Each arm appears to be emitting a laser effect, which results in the shape of the Riven icon in between the three arms. 
RIVEN EXPANSION: RIVEN SPLICING
The second half of our Riven Expansion arrives: Riven Splicing!

With the use of Riven Splicers, obtained exclusively from The Icebind gamemode, specific traits can be combined to create all-new spliced traits! When selecting a Riven Mod, a new Riven Splicing menu will appear. Opening this menu will display all owned Rivens, detailing which Rivens have valid trait combinations.

Select any lit up Riven Mod to see which traits can be spliced! 

Image Description: A view of the new Riven Splicing menu. On the left side of the screen is a list of Rivens, with incompatible Rivens grayed out with a “No Compatible Traits” label on top of them. The right side of the screen shows the possible Splicing options for the Selected Riven, in this case a Hikou Riven. The screen offers the choice to merge +88.5% zoom and -222.6% Damage traits into a +285.1% Weakpoint Trait and a ??? Trait. 

Spliced traits require a combination of two specific traits to splice together, with different combinations creating different outcomes! Combinations are pre-selected and confirmation is required before applying a spliced trait to your Riven. We have listed all combinations at the bottom of this section, and you can view the combinations possible on a specific Riven with the “Show All Possible Splices” option in the Riven Splicing menu. This means you’ll always know what spliced trait you’re about to receive before you make a decision. 

If multiple spliced traits are available from a single Riven Mod, a “Change Selected Trait” option appears, allowing you to choose which spliced trait you want! 

As an example: A Riven Mod with +Heat Damage, +Cold Damage, and +Toxin damage will have 3 spliced traits to choose from: +Blast Damage, +Gas Damage, and +Viral Damage. Which spliced trait goes on the Riven Mod is your choice!


Image Description: A pop-up for deciding which Trait to Splice. The options provided are “Weak Point Damage” or “Weak Point Critical Chance”

When traits are spliced, the two required traits are consumed, with the spliced trait AND a second random trait taking their place. The random trait is one you may receive from cycling normally, including one just used in making the spliced trait, with one change. If one of the consumed traits was a negative bonus, the random trait will also be a negative; if both consumed traits were positive, it will be a positive. This ensures your Riven keeps the same layout of positive and negative traits it has before combining! 

After splicing, the total number of positive and negative traits will no longer change on the Riven Mod, no matter how many times it is cycled after the fact. This can be undone by removing the spliced trait from the Riven.


Image: The end-result of a successful Riven Splicing. A Hikou Riven Mod is in the center of the screen, featuring the new +274.1% Weak Point Damage trait, as well as the random -188.3% Damage trait. 

Once a spliced trait is on your Riven, it’s there to stay! It is locked, but is not considered a locked trait — meaning it will not double your Kuva cost. Should you ever decide to remove the trait, the lock can be removed and the spliced trait can be cycled off, allowing a new trait to be spliced on! Utilize both a spliced trait and trait locking to lock two traits at once, making cycling for the last trait or two you want even easier.

As an example: Let’s say you had a Riven Mod with 3 Positive Traits and 0 Negative traits, and chose a + Viral spliced trait. No matter how many times the Riven is cycled, it retains +Viral Damage and 2 other positive traits, with 0 negative traits. You could even lock one of the other traits, guaranteeing two traits and cycling for the perfect final trait!


Image Description: A view of the Riven Cycle screen displaying a Spliced Hikou Riven Mod. The Mod has two locked traits: one of them is the Spliced Trait (+274.1% Weak Point Damage), and another is a locked trait via the Trait Locking system (in this case, +164.3% Critical Chance). The cost to cycle this Riven is 7,000 Kuva, which is doubled as a result of the locked Critical Chance trait.

The full list of spliced traits and which traits are needed to obtain them can be found below.


 

Ranged Weapons (Rifle, Shotgun, Pistol, Kitgun, Archgun, Select Companion Rivens):

  • Weakpoint Damage
    • Damage & Zoom
    • Damage & Multishot
  • Weakpoint Critical Chance
    • Critical Chance & Zoom
    • Critical Chance & Multishot
  • Ammo Efficiency
    • Magazine Capacity & Reload Speed
    • Weapon Recoil & Ammo Maximum
  • Magazine Reload While Holstered
    • Ammo Maximum & Reload Speed
    • Ammo Maximum & Magazine Capacity
  • Status Damage
    • Damage & Status Chance

 


 

Melee Weapons (Melee, Zaw, Select Companion Rivens):

  • Heavy Attack Damage
    • Heavy Attack Efficiency & Additional Combo Count Chance
  • Heavy Attack Windup Speed
    • Heavy Attack Efficiency & Combo Duration
  • Parry Angle
    • Attack Speed & Range
  • Slam Damage
    • Melee Damage & Attack Speed
  • Status Damage
    • Melee Damage & Status Chance

 


 

All Rivens:

  • Gas Damage
    • Toxin Damage & Heat Damage
  • Corrosive Damage
    • Toxin Damage & Electric Damage
  • Viral Damage
    • Toxin Damage & Cold Damage
  • Radiation Damage
    • Heat Damage & Electric Damage
  • Blast Damage
    • Heat Damage & Cold Damage
  • Magnetic Damage
    • Electric Damage & Cold Damage
  • Damage vs Orokin
    • Damage vs Corpus & Damage vs Grineer
  • Damage vs Techrot
    • Damage vs Corpus & Damage vs Infested
  • Damage vs Scaldra
    • Damage vs Infested & Damage vs Grineer

For feedback on our Riven Splicing system, please use the dedicated Riven Expansion subforum. 

ADDITIONS

  • Added the following items to Cephalon Melica’s Classroom Supplies:
    • Glacial Laboratory Captura Scene
    • Tethyan Parchment Tatters decorations
      • Each individual Tatter is available separately, ensuring you can obtain whichever Tatter(s) you want.
  • Added the Complexion B-17 [Legacy] to the Drifter/Operator Complexion menu.
    • This Complexion allows players to access the original implementation of Vitiligo, before its changes with the Iceblade of Narin.

CHANGES

  • Players can now purchase 1 Riven Slot for 20 Platinum (instead of 3 for 60). 
    • Previously, players could only purchase Riven Slots in bundles of 3. The 3 Riven Slot bundle has been removed and replaced with the single purchase option.
    • Following a Nightwave issue last year, affected players received an extra Riven Slot, which meant they were prevented from reaching the Riven Slot cap. Now, players can purchase Riven Slots in whatever number they desire (unless that number exceeds the cap). 
  • Excavators and Defense Objectives (ex: Mobile Defense terminals, Defense Targets, etc.) now have a 90% damage reduction against Blitz Eximus shockwave attacks.
    • Defense Objectives now also benefit from shieldgating (like Excavators, which received this change with The Shadowgrapher).
  • Entropic Eximus can no longer spawn as Helions, as their flying behaviour can make them difficult to target with melee weapons.
  • Reduced the currency cost for Kuva bundles across various Vendors:
    • Acrithis’ Wares: 
      • Increased to 10,000 Kuva for 10 Pathos Clamps (was 5,000 for 10).
    • Exchange Scuttler Husks (Acrithis): 
      • Increased to 14,000 Kuva for 25 Scuttler Husks (was 6,000 for 100).
      • Also increased purchase limit from one to three per week.
    • Flare’s Memorabilia:
      • Increased to 14,000 Kuva for 100 Heartstrings (was 6,000 for 100)
      • Reduced purchase limit from seven to three times per week. 
    • Nightcap’s Wares:
      • Increased to 14,000 Kuva for 75 Fergolyte (was 7,000 for 75)
      • Reduced purchase limit from six to three times per week.  
    • Hunhow’s Keepsakes:
      • Increased to 17,000 Kuva for 35 of both Emerald & Crimson Talents (was 7,000 for 35).
      • Reduced purchase limit from seven to three per week.
  • The Events tab in the Navigation menu now sorts recurring events by most recently started.
  • Reduced the amount of space the Thermia Fractures event takes up in the World State Window on the Navigation console.
  • Updated the Entropic Kuva's resource description to specify it drops from Entropic Eximus.
  • Added the Shedu Day of the Dead Skin to the Nightwave Cred Offerings rotation.

Performance and Optimizations

  • Improved performance issues related to Oberon's Smite.
  • Improved performance issues related to Frost's Avalanche.
  • Fixed minor performance issues related to Last Gasp.
  • Optimized texture streaming memory usage.

TOP FIXES

  • Metal Shader Fixes:
    • Improvements and fixes towards our Metal Shaders are ongoing. For more information on the limitations related to updating Metal Shaders, please read our official post. 
    • Fixed metallics appearing plasticy for players with High Shader Quality toggled off.
    • Fixes towards certain Warframe Skins appearing light gray when tinted black following our High Shader Quality changes.
  • Fixed Oberon's Renewal no longer slowing bleedout timers.
  • Fixed not being able to use Loki's Switch Teleport on Hacked Drones in the Plains of Eidolon.
  • Fixed Balor Fomorian events not being scheduled properly, resulting in repeated Razorback Armadas.
    • The pending Balor Fomorian will begin once the current Razorback Armada has concluded.
  • Fixed Grendel's Gastroparesis causing Azima's alternate fire to stack Secondary Enervate infinitely.
  • Fixed the "Hide Owned" toggle hiding different items each time it was toggled on and off.
  • Fixed being unable to upgrade Companions via the Navigation Loadout bar if Orion is set as the Primary Son.
  • Fixed Shotgun Rivens being listed as "Shotgun" instead of the actual weapon when chatlinked.
  • Tentative fix towards cases of controller inputs not functioning correctly when using Steam Input.

Fixes

  • Fixed the Aksondol and Nunchasa missing blueprint location descriptions in the Market.
  • Fixed moving very slowly resulting in Mining Deposits not updating properly when using Oxylus' Scan Matter precept.
  • Fixed the Caliban Scion Helmet's metallics and base color not matching base Caliban.
  • Fixed a duplicate Catenach appearing when using Uriel in Duviri.
  • Fixed the Operator being able to attempt to pull out the Iceblade of Narin.
  • Fixed camera flickering if a movement input is pressed when attempting to pull Narin's Iceblade free.
  • Fixed players in Yuvan Peak blocking the screen when attempting to pull out Narin's Iceblade.
  • Fixed Tauron Strike animations being broken if cast while Narin's Nuranarmin is active.
  • Fixed a texture issue on Yuvan Peak.
  • Fixed Uriel's Demons being doubled after using Transference.
  • Fixed duplicates of Uriel's Demons appearing in the Höllvania Central Mall Backrooms Scene if Uriel is also equipped on the Loadout Display.
  • Fixed having two full-body Sigils applied resulting in the Sigils' effects not applying to the head.
  • Fixed the Mission Tutorial Transmission toggle hiding introduction transmissions for the Temporal and Deep Archimedea missions.
  • Fixed Gemini Skin faces becoming distorted when swapping in and out of Duviri Navigation in the Navigation menu.
  • Fixed an unnecessary "Mission 1" appearing over the Hallowed Nightmares alert in the Navigation menu.
  • Fixed incorrect capitalization for Voidshell Materials in the Operator/Drifter customization screen.
  • Fixed a rare case of Inaros being revived with function loss if he died at the start of casting Sandstorm with an item (ex: power cell) in his hands.
  • Fixed a sound crash.

Script Error Fixes
Script errors mean that something went wrong when the game client was executing a script, which can have various outcomes. Usually it means the related content didn’t function properly under specific circumstances — often we don’t actually know what the error outcome was, so we list it as a Script Error fix to indicate it was addressing an unintended behaviour.

  • Fixed a script error when attempting to destroy an Entropic Eximus’ shield.
  • Fixed a script error related to Narin's Nuranarim.
  • Fixed a script error related to Nokko's Sporespring projectiles.
  • Fixed a script error related to the Unairu Tauron Strike.
  • Fixed a script error related to Nightwave Act popups when transitioning out of missions on the Zariman Ten Zero.
  • Fixed a script error related to the Panic Call Peely Pix in Temporal Archimedea.
  • Fixed a script error related to Narin's passive.
  • Fixed a script error related to Baruuk's Serene Storm.
  • Fixed a script error related to the Confront Kullervo objective in Duviri.
  • Fixed a script error related to Khora's Venari.
  • Fixed a script related to Arcane effects that trigger "on Critical Hit".
  • Fixed a script error related to Yareli's Sea Snares.

For a list of known issues that are on our radar, visit our dedicated thread: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1523875-known-issues-iceblade-of-narin/

item.title: Update 44: Iceblade of Narin
item.description:
Image Description: The Iceblade of Narin art features Narin in motion looking towards the frozen monolith at the Yuvan Peak.

UPDATE 44: ICEBLADE OF NARIN

At the summit of a familiar peak on Earth — the place you first mastered your Void powers — a mysterious frozen monument has taken shape, prompting strange happenings aboard the Zariman and a new threat from the Man in the Wall…

Return to where you were presented with the decision to destroy, control or consume a powerful elixir: Yuvan Peak! Visit the dark side of Earth and enter a unique hub. At this spectacular mountain summit, you'll find Narin's Crest and Neote, Narin’s legendary sword, encased firmly in the ice. Marvel at its wonder and attempt to pull Narin’s Iceblade free. 

Cephalon Melica has also been summoned to Yuvan’s Peak, but unfortunately not for a fun field trip. Entropy threatens the Zariman, and Narin’s influence on the Peak is key to stopping its spread. Collect Entropic Kuva from Entropic Eximus found on the Zariman, and exchange it with Melica to contain it. In doing so, you’ll receive items from her wares, including Narin’s blueprints!

Our 66th Warframe, Narin, also descends in swirling eddies in this update! Her blade keen and deadly as an icy wind. She wields ice to heal and defend as deftly as her swift rapier strikes. Trade Entropic Kuva to Cephalon Melica for Narin’s blueprints, as well as the blueprints to craft her signature weapons’ Nunchasa and Aksondol. 

The crystalline citadel ascends, Citrine Prime Access is here! Move through the battlefield with refined radiance with Citrine Prime, Steflos Prime, Corufell Prime and her Prime Accessories. Purchase Citrine Prime Access Packs or earn this brilliant gem of a Prime Warframe and her weapons by cracking Relics.

Two new Deluxe Skin Collections are here to make the ground shake! Qorvex Basilica and Banshee Threnodia arrive with a collection of cosmetics fit for those looking to strike terror in the most fashionable of ways. Speaking of Banshee, our sound Warframe, has received a full rework to make her a truly lethal presence not only heard but felt on the battlefield. 

Iceblade of Narin is packed with so much more! Including Riven Trait Locking, new Warframe Augments for Oraxia, Uriel, Frost, and Grendel, new Atragraph Mods for Banshee and Baruuk, new TennoGen, improved hair shaders and metal tinting, Archimedea Parameter & Reward track QOL and so much more!  
 

Image Description: Banshee poses with glowing arms outstretched. To her right from top to bottom are the Warframe logo, Free Banshee Login Reward, and the dates of the promotion of September 23 to October 7. 

Free Login Rewards

Log into Warframe from Sept 23rd @ 11:30 AM ET to Oct 7th @ 11:59 PM ET to claim Banshee and one built Forma* for FREE and experience her new Ability Rework for yourself! Learn more about her rework in the dedicated section. 

*Once the Free Banshee inbox expires, you can still claim the Forma (if you had not already received the Banshee inbox) on login until December 31, 2026.  

Upcoming Content & Events 

Iceblade of Narin is followed by the listed content below coming in the near future: 

Image Description: Six Warframes stand poised for battle within a frosty cave with the Warframe logo and Glacial Defiance: New 6 Player Missions in the foreground. From left to right we can see: Wisp, Rhino, Volt, Excalibur, Mesa, and Mag.

  • Glacial Defiance (New 6-Player game mode) – Releasing sometime before or on October 15th 
    • To learn more about the Glacial Defiance launch timing and the reasons behind the staggered release, please read our official PSA here: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1523427-psa-glacial-defiance-release-window/
  • Riven Splicing - Coming with Glacial Defiance launch 
    • The item required to perform Riven Splicing, the Riven Splicer, is rewarded from Glacial Defiance. So once the gamemode launches, Splicing will also become available! 

Image Description: Epoch Operation: Taubound art that features gold lettering for Taubound and the Warframe logo against a dark backdrop of space.

  • Epoch Operation: Taubound – Begins October 15th! 
    • Arturos and Zioa have lain dormant long enough: the time to assume control of your Vessel is almost at hand. With new worlds and possibilities beyond the Origin System closer than ever, your window to prepare for the journey to Tau begins now, ahead of a never-before-seen, once in a lifetime Epoch Operation this October. Learn more here: https://www.warframe.com/en/news/epoch-operation-taubound

 

Update 44 is a Mainline Update! 

Meaning that everything the team has been working on since the launch of Update 43: Jade Shadows: Constellations is in this update (with the obvious exception of content that is not ready to be released). It is very likely, as it is with all Mainline updates, that things slip through the cracks so we will be watching for bug reports and feedback in the dedicated Iceblade of Narin subforums to address in follow-up Hotfixes.

If any of the terms above are new to you, visit The Warframe Lexicon for Updates to learn more about Warframe’s development cycle. 
 

Download Sizes:

  • PC DirectX 11: ~7.83 GB*
  • PC DirectX 12: ~8 GB*

*Sound Optimization
You may notice a larger download size with this update due to optimization of our sound files. This requires you to download new versions of the files that when patched into your installation will result in a smaller install footprint overall without compromising any audio quality. 

 

Image Description: Yuvan Peak sits in tranquility with several pillars adorned by talismans and ice. Somewhat in the distance we can see a Warframe standing near a frozen monolith with a pale blue glow.

NEW EARTH RELAY: YUVAN PEAK

Attention students! It’s time for a field trip.

Cephalon Melica has been summoned to Yuvan Peak on Earth. This familiar site is now transformed by Narin’s influence — her glacial Crest glitters against the snow. Within this frozen monument lies her Iceblade: Neote. Perhaps you’ll be the one to pull it free. 

 

Video Description: GIF showing the rotation effect when selecting the Yuvan Peak node on Earth. The camera pans around Lua and reveals the other side of Earth where Yuvan Peak is the lone visible node.

This trip is not all fun, however. Entropic Kuva is seeping into the Zariman, and Yuvan Peak holds the key to help stop its threat. 

Prerequisites: To access Yuvan Peak, players must have completed both the Angels of the Zariman and Whispers in the Walls quest. 

In this new Hub, gain access to the following:

  • New Vendor: Cephalon Melica
    • For more information on her wares, please visit her dedicated section below. 
  • Coming Soon: Glacial Defiance (New 6-Player Game Mode) 
    • This content is not yet released, but Yuvan Peak will be where you can start these missions. Learn more about general release window and the reasoning behind the delay: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1523427-psa-glacial-defiance-release-window/
  • Narin’s Iceblade in Narin’s Crest

 

Image Description: A closeup of Narin’s Crest, a single sword stuck in a frozen pillar. Framing it are two large curved ice structures, a snowy path littered with stones, and vast white clouds in the distance.

Narin’s Crest 

On Yuvan Peak, Neote, Narin’s Iceblade, can be found frozen solid in a mound of ice, anchored firmly. Who will be the one to pull Neote from Narin’s Crest? 

 

Image Description: Narin stands in front of Cephalon Melica on the snowy Yuvan Peak. A “Cephalon Melica” context action is visible. 

New Vendor: Cephalon Melica

Oh, students! A familiar face is eager to greet you once you have made it to the Yuvan Peak. Concerned with the effects that Entropy is having aboard the Zariman, Cephalon Melica requires your assistance in containing its spread. Collect Entropic Kuva and bring it to Cephalon Melica and she may provide you with knowledge and supplies in exchange.

You may chat with Cephalon Melica at either Yuvan Peak or in the Chrysalith (can be accessed through Fast Travel) to browse her Classroom Supplies and see what she offers:

  • Narin’s Main and Component Blueprints
  • Nunchasa’s Main and Component Blueprints
  • Aksondol’s Main and Component Blueprints
  • On Wings of Ice Honoria
  • Narin Prex Card
  • New Somachord Tracks:
    • Neote’s Dance
    • Ice Speaker
  • New Captura Scenes:
    • Melica’s Laboratory Scene
    • Yuvan Peak Scene
  • Glacium Sigil
  • Seonang Ephemera
  • Tidon Shoulder Medallion
  • Tidon Chest Medallion
  • Tidon Leg Medallion
  • Niveus Sumdali
  • Niveus Nepheri Skin
  • Niveus Dark Split-Sword Skin

  • Dealing melee damage with the Iceblade of Narin buff from Neote on Yuvan Peak will break the bubble if either the bubble or the Entropic Eximus is struck.
  • Tauron strikes will break the bubble upon contact.

RIVEN EXPANSION: TRAIT LOCKING (LIVE) & RIVEN SPLICING (COMING SOON)

You may have already seen a sneak preview of these new systems in our Dev Workshop. With today’s launch, Trait Locking is officially live and Riven Splicing will be coming soon with the release of Glacial Defiance! Read on below for the latest on these systems. 

Riven Mods (often just called “Rivens” for short) were introduced in 2016, and are nearly a decade old now! With this update we’ve added a new feature for Rivens: Trait Locking! A second new feature will join Glacial Defiance: Riven Splicing. We’ll share a little information about Riven Splicing below, for a more detailed preview of the system you can check out our Dev Workshop.

 

TRAIT LOCKING (LIVE) 

One of the primary requests we’ve received for Riven Mods is to allow players to lock a stat to prevent it from being Cycled. Now, you can do so with a system called Trait Locking! 

One trait (stat) can be locked at a time while cycling a Riven, freezing it until the lock is removed or the Cycling menu is closed. 

There is no cost or item required to lock a trait. Locks can be removed and re-added for free! However, when cycling a Riven Mod with a locked trait, the Kuva cost is doubled. Locking a trait is entirely optional, and Rivens can still be cycled as usual without a lock.

How to Lock a Riven Trait:

1. Go to the Mod Segment in your Base of Operations

2. Select the Riven Mod you’d like to cycle and select the “Cycle Riven” option 

3. Select the “Lock Trait” button

Image Description: Screenshot of the Riven Mod UI showing the Soma Argicron Mod. The options for Lock Trait and Cycle for 3,500 Kuva are shown and the cursor is hovering on Lock Trait.

4. Select the trait you wish to lock. The locked trait will appear greyed out with a lock icon on the Mod and will also be listed above the “Lock Trait” button.

Image Description: Screenshot of the Choose A Trait To Lock UI screen. Two traits are displayed as options, the first is a 1.5 times Damage to Grineer, and the second is an increased Critical Chance by 167.2%.

Image Description: Screenshot of the Riven Mod UI screen showing the Soma Argircon Mod with a locked trait denoted by a lock icon. Above the Lock Trait option is the currently locked trait of increased Critical Chance by 167.2% and a remove icon next to it.

5. Begin cycling your Riven with the locked trait! Notice that once locked, it will not change while cycling.

Image Description: Screenshot of the Riven Mod Cycling UI at the Cycle preview screen. We can see that the Riven Mod has a locked trait and the resulting cycled Mod retains the locked trait.


It is important to note that a trait needs to be re-locked each time you open this menu, as they are not maintained once the menu has been closed. 

Cycling a Riven with a locked trait prevents the number of traits on the Mod from changing. This means a Mod with 3 positive traits and 1 negative trait will always cycle into another version with 3 positive traits and 1 negative trait if one of the traits is locked. To cycle into a different number of traits, unlock all traits and cycle again.

 

RIVEN SPLICING (LAUNCHING AT A LATER DATE WITH GLACIAL DEFIANCE) 

Riven Splicing combines two traits on a Riven together to form a new spliced trait which is then locked on the Riven (without consuming a Trait Lock). Riven Splicing will require Riven Splicers, which will be rewarded from Glacial Defiance when it releases sometime before or on October 15 (release window PSA for more info). For more details about Riven Splicing, refer to our Dev Workshop.

Image Description: Banshee blasts surrounding enemies with her arms outstretched sending them flying. A soft light is emitted from her hands providing the only light source in the dark room she stands in.

BANSHEE REWORK 

Banshee may not be at the top of your Loadout list, but those who have mastered her kit are able to deal a significant amount of damage in-mission. While not the flashiest pick, she can turn any weapon into something truly lethal — our goal is to maintain that lethality, while adding a few quality of life lifts to her Abilities. The following changes aim to make her kit feel fluid and impactful, while staying true to her identity as a sound-based Warframe.

Passive

Banshee’s Passive is helpful to a sect of players who value stealth, but largely has little effect in most missions. We are keeping her hush mechanic, but adding a little extra value that feels thematically appropriate for our sound-based Warframe. 

  • Banshee’s abilities pierce the ears of nearby enemies. Casting abilities applies maximum Puncture Status on foes within 10m. 
  • Banshee’s weapon noises are hushed.

 

First Ability - Sonic Boom

Sonic Boom is an excellent survival tool for Banshee, but its ragdoll mechanic does not synergize well with other elements of her kit. The following changes help improve its synergy, and improve Banshee’s overall survivability. 

  • Sonic Boom is now cast one-handed and no longer roots Banshee in place.
  • Removed Ragdoll from affected enemies — now pushes them back and stuns them.
    • The ragdoll did not synergize well with Sonar as it made it harder to target the weakpoints.
  • Increased Impact damage from 50 to 250.
  • Sonic Boom now reduces 70% of Armor, scaling with Ability Strength up to 100%. 
    • This mechanic was originally tied to Sonic Fracture, but is now part of her base kit.
  • Sonic Boom now breaks resource containers and breakable decorations.
  • Sonic Boom now deals a guaranteed Impact Status Effect. 
  • Renamed the “Strength” stat to “Push Force”, as it affects how strongly Sonic Boom will push enemies. 

 Sonic Fracture Augment

  • Renamed to “Sonic Siphon”. 
  • Banshee gains Armor for 20s if an enemy is hit by Sonic Siphon, up to a cap of 1500 Armor.
    • Armor does not need to be stripped for this bonus Armor to apply!
  • Recasting Sonic Siphon will refresh the Bonus Armor duration if an enemy is struck by the cast.

 

Second Ability - Sonar

Sonar turns many weapons into a powerhouse in the right hands, but requires a lot of spam casting to reach its full potential. In addition, it offers little synergy with existing Weak Point enhancements as Sonar’s Weak Spots are considered a separate mechanic. These changes address common player feedback, while also giving the ability a light quality of life lift. 

  • Sonar’s Weak Spots are now considered Weak Points, giving them synergy with a variety of Mods, Arcanes, and more. 
  • Sonar now prioritizes unmarked parts of the body for its Weak Spots to help with Weak Spot legibility. 
    • The reticle now turns red when shooting at the Weak Spots, just like other Weak Points. 
  • Casting Sonar no longer roots Banshee in place. 
  • Updated SFX when hitting a Weak Spot.

Resonance Augment

  • Unchanged.

 

Third Ability - Silence

Silence is a powerful Ability, but its impact on the battlefield is not always clear to players. The following changes help improve the visibility of its effects, with a few quality of life touches!

  • Silence can now be recast to reset its duration and reapply the Stun.
  • Casting Silence no longer roots Banshee in place. 
  • Improved VFX on enemies to make it clearer they are affected by Silence. 

Savage Silence Augment

  • Unchanged.

 

Fourth Ability - Sound Quake

Sound Quake is an iconic part of Banshee’s kit, but it struggles to synergize with her other Abilities. Our goal with the following changes is to make Sound Quake fit more fluidly into Banshee’s playstyle, while retaining the nostalgic elements that are emblematic of her kit.

  • Sound Quake is no longer channelled. Casting the ability creates an area of effect with a duration of 25 seconds.
  • Resonating Quake fans may be confused by this change — we are swapping the mechanics of the Augment and the base Ability to make Sound Quake synergize better with the rest of Banshee’s kit. 
  • Banshee is briefly invulnerable when casting Sound Quake. 
  • Enemies receive guaranteed Blast Status Effects while in Sound Quake’s area of effect, which reduces based on distance from the center. 
  • Increased casting animation speed to make it more fluid.
  • Sound Quake now breaks containers within its entire area of effect, not just the 5 metres around the epicenter.

Resonating Quake Augment

  • Renamed to “Gaseous Quake”.
  • Gaseous Quake is now a channelled Ability, which takes on the mechanic of Banshee’s old Sound Quake. 
  • Banshee is rooted in place to channel Gaseous Quake, which deals additional Gas Damage and Status Effects to enemies in the area of effect. 
  • Gaseous Quake’s damage is multiplied every second during cast, up to a cap.
    • Energy drain also increases every second during casting. 
  • Gaseous Quake's area of effect now persists for a short duration after channelling ends.    
  • Improved Line of Sight now applies to Gaseous Quake.
  • Updated VFX and SFX to reflect this new gassy styling of the Ability.

OPERATOR/DRIFTER IMPROVEMENTS

Hair Shader Improvements

We’ve improved the quality of our hair shaders with the goal of having richer colors and better visuals. Here’s what the team’s efforts have resulted in and what you can expect: 

  • Black hair is a much “truer” black, and less a “mid grey” 
  • Colored hair is deeper and more accurate to selected color 
  • White hair looks more white without losing depth
  • Sheen is stronger but balanced with underlying color
  • Added a slight rimlight on hair for “scattering”

While these changes are a major overall lift to hair shaders, you may have to make some adjustments to find your preferred look once more. At the same time, you may enjoy experimenting with the shaders and achieving looks that might not have been possible before, so have fun exploring new options! 

Image Description: Composite image of a live build and dev build screenshot showcasing the difference in sheen and color on an Operator’s black hairstyle. In the live build the black hair has a grey tone compared to the dev build which has a deeper black. 

Note: All color channels are set to the “blackest” black from the Smoke palette! 

Image Description: Composite image of a live build and dev build screenshot showcasing the difference in a deep red hair color on an Operator. In the live build the deep red appears lighter than the selected color whereas the dev build is more accurate.

Image Description: Composite image of a live build and dev build screenshot showcasing the difference in highlights in an Operator’s hairstyle. The dev build changes feature the dimensions of the bright colors. 

Image Description: Composite image of a live build and dev build screenshot showcasing the difference in visual fidelity of hair on an Operator with blonde and pink hair. The live build’s hair appears more muted while the dev build has a richer gradient in colors adding more depth.

 

These changes also apply to Kubrow fur! 

Image Description: Composite image of a live build and dev build screenshot showcasing the difference in fur presentation on a Kubrow. In the live build the greys and blacks appear gray along with the blue being brighter than the dev build where each color is richer and deeper.

As a general note, we’ve also made a handful of small improvements to Operator and Drifter cosmetics and hair texture. We’ve also improved tint options to certain hairstyles that were previously not very customizable (ex: Short Sidecut, Kaya’s Hairstyle).   

While in the pursuit of improving the shaders, we also acknowledge the effort that is dedicated to customizing your Operator and Drifter. So we’ll be watching for your feedback on these changes. Thank you, Tenno!  
 

Vitiligo Complexion Changes

Image Description: Screenshot of the Drifter Features UI menu with the vitiligo complexion, Complexion B-17 selected. Two additional options are present, Markings Coverage and Invert Markings.
 

With this update we are changing the way that the vitiligo complexion, Complexion B-17, functions. Previously, the skin tone selected via Complexion Tint would apply across the entire skin and this would lead to unexpected tones or the erasure of vitiligo in some tone choices. 

Now Complexion Tint applies only to melanated areas which allows for a better tinting overall and greater respect for the tone selected. Through the addition of two new features we have expanded your ability to customize your skin tone with vitiligo.

  • Markings Coverage: Lets you adjust the degree to which the vitiligo pattern is present (i.e. the dispersion of melanin)
    • Note: In order for this option to become available, you must first select a complexion tint. 
  • Invert Markings: Lets you swap the current melanated vs lack of melanin regions within the vitiligo pattern

 Video Description: GIF of the Drifter Features UI showing the effect of changing the Markings Coverage slider on the vitiligo pattern. The Invert Markings toggle is then turned on and off to show the swap in melanated and non-melanted areas.

We hope these changes allow you to better shape and express your Operator/Drifter in the way you would like!

 

QUALITY OF LIFE (QOL) CHANGES

Weak Point Standardization

With our changes to Banshee’s Sonar, we are working on a wider standardization of Weak Points. There are a variety of Abilities and enhancements that trigger “On Headshot”, but enemies have a variety of weak points outside of just their heads (if they even have a head, depending on the enemy). As a result, we are working to convert all “On Headshot” triggers to be “On Weakpoint” instead. This is a large undertaking considering the vast array of Incarnons, Mods, Arcanes, Unique Traits, and more, so we’re prioritizing the most popular enhancements to start.

Converted the following triggers from “On Headshot” to “On Weakpoint”:

  • Longbow Sharpshot
  • Argon Scope
  • Hydraulic Crosshairs
  • Galvanized Crosshairs
  • Galvanized Scope
  • Primary Deadhead
  • Secondary Deadhead
  • Arcane Precision
  • Arcane Pistoleer
  • Sharpshooter

Metal Tint Improvements 

Similar to our hair shaders, there’s been a longstanding issue with dark tinted metals appearing grey. We have fixed this for Iceblade of Narin by making changes to the encoding to achieve richer and more saturated metals. Where the current system has a difficult time honoring your chosen tint on metal channels, this new one should more accurately reflect the selected color.

The Perita Rebellion Mine Rework

While traversing the battlefield of The Perita Rebellion, you may have encountered small interactable mines which pose environmental hazards. We have made a few changes to these mines to prevent accidental activation, reduce aiming complexity, and to encourage using melee rather than shooting them.

Mines will now:

  • No longer spawn on top of each other and cannot spawn inside of the larger mines from the Clear the Minefield Order
  • Have a light that blinks to identify that it is a mine and the light’s blinking increases the closer your proximity to the mine
  • Rise up from the ground into melee attack height once a player enters within their activation proximity
  • Prioritize targets based on where your crosshair is pointing when attempting to melee them

CHANGES

Archimedea Parameter & Reward Track Changes

Archimedea is changing! A variety of changes are coming to the choices a Tenno makes before starting an Archimedea (both Deep Archimedea and Temporal Archimedea, including their Elite versions) mission. 

Arsenal Bonuses

Warframes and Weapons alike will be granted an Arsenal Boost for matching their respective Individual Parameters! The buff received will be the same for each parameter, meaning regardless which Primary Weapon you choose, the boost is the same! Pick the Weapon or Warframe that works best with each boost for maximum efficiency!

Image Description: Screenshot of the Deep Archimedea UI screen showing the Individual Parameters, Missions, Research Points Track, and Current Loadout. Specific elements of the Individual Parameters are highlighted that match the current loadout.

 

Reward Track Changes

We’re moving around a few of the rewards at the top end of the Elite Archimedea Reward Tracks, and adding a new reward!

  • A new reward is added at 34 points, consisting of Vosfor or Pix Chips, for Deep Archimedea or Temporal Archimedea respectively
  • The Legendary reward at 34 points has been moved to 37 points
  • The final reward at 37 points has been moved to 40 points

Image Description: Composite image of before and after the update to Archimedea’s Research Points Reward Track. In the after image we can see a change in the rewards at 34 and 37 points and the addition of a reward at 40.

 

Warframe Research Point Changes

Studious Tenno may have noticed that the 40 points now required for maximum rewards is higher than the current maximum! Worry not, we’re also increasing the amount of points from using one of the 3 Warframes under Individual Parameters - they will now grant 3 Research Points per mission, up from 1! This raises the maximum amount of points in one Elite Archimedea mission to 43.

The highest tier reward (at 40 points) will now be obtainable without one Individual Parameter (other than Warframe), and the Legendary reward is achievable whilst leaving behind two Individual Parameters!

Additional Personal Modifiers

Six new Personal Modifiers have been added to the rotation to keep you on your toes! 

  • Infected Wounds: Gain a Toxin Status Effect every time you take damage.
  • Anemic Shields: Maximum shield and overshield will not exceed 500.
  • Shortened Reach: Ability range reduced by 50% 
  • No Pets Allowed: Companions are disabled.
    • Note: When playing Khora, this does not disable Venari.
  • Channeled Greed: While a channeled ability is active, maximum shields and overshields are reduced each second. 10s cooldown to fully recover.
  • Low Yield: Blast radius of weapons with radial attacks set to 3m

Plus one change to an existing Personal Modifier:

  • Framecurse Syndrome: Activating an Ability inflicts 50 damage and 150 shield damage upon you. 
    • Added the damage to shields

General Changes

  • Sirius & Orion can now be rolled as an option in Duviri.

  • Necramech Slots have been retired! 
    • Moving forward, players will only be able to own one of each of the Necramechs (Voidrig & Bonewidow). Those who already owned multiple before this update will keep them. 
    • We will be running a script sometime after the update has launched to refund players who had purchased Necramech Slots. We will update you once the script has completed! We will update you once the script has completed! 
  • Umbra now has a proper boss-type health bar in a certain stage of The Sacrifice quest.
